Definition: from G5199; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine):--be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).
BiblicalUsage: hygiaínō turns up where the Bible says to be sound, to be in good health. In Luke 5:31, the text says "They that are whole need not a physician." In 1 Timothy 1:10, the text says "and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine."
TheologicalSignificance: hygiaínō convinces me that healing is God's work, in His time and His way, and He is able. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
